messages:
Tom (sales): Heads-up: enterprise prospect wants a 12mo commit but their workload is mixed. Daytime: embedding pipeline ~12k req/min (short, 64 tokens). Evening: chat bursts 150-300 QPS with 400-1200 token tails. They want guidance for reserved GPUs vs autoscale.

Nina (acct-eng): They also asked whether embedding workers and chat can share the same Dedicated pool, or if we should carve separate pools. Cost-sensitivity is high.

Tomas (solutions): Short answer: you can colocate if you size for the combined token throughput and enforce per-route quotas. But mixing increases variance; I'd recommend logical partitioning (routes) with shared commit + reserved isolates if needed.

Wei (eng-runtime): For math: embeddings are cheap per-request but high QPS. Quick numbers: embeddings: 12k/min = 200 rps * 64 tokens = 12.8k tokens/sec. Chat baseline 100 rps * 300 tokens = 30k tokens/sec, occasional spikes to 300 rps * 800 tokens = 240k tokens/sec (ephemeral).

Tomas (solutions): Our measured token throughput per A100-like GPU after 4-bit quant = ~1400-1800 tokens/sec for mixed batch sizes; long sequences drop that. Use conservative 1400 tps/GPU for mixed workload.

Wei (eng-runtime): So rough capacity calc:
```
- steady tokens/sec = embeddings(12800) + chat_baseline(30000) = 42800 tps
- GPUs steady = ceil(42800 / 1400) = 31 GPUs
- peak transient tokens/sec = embeddings + chat_peak(240000) = 252800 tps
- GPUs peak = ceil(252800 / 1400) = 181 GPUs (transient!)
```
We obviously can't reserve that many. Need burst strategy and graceful degradation.

Tom (sales): 31 GPUs steady seems large. Customer hoped for ~10-12 reserved. What's alternative?

Tomas (solutions): Options: 1) reserve lower baseline and rely on burst credits + prewarm + model-level fallbacks; 2) push quantized smaller chat model for bursts; 3) split embedding workers into cheaper CPU-backed or smaller GPU nodes with batching to lower GPU token pressure.

Nina (acct-eng): Can we show them a hybrid commit: reserve 12 GPUs (guaranteed), have 6 prewarmed instances (charged partially), burst credit pool to add up to 50 GPUs for 120s, and autoscale to 120 GPUs if billing approved?

Wei (eng-runtime): That seems reasonable. With 12 reserved + 6 prewarm (prewarm ~= 25-35% cost of full), expected steady headroom: 18 GPUs * 1400 = 25.2k tps. We still need to throttle or route very long chat sessions to quantized fallback. So we recommend per-route max tokens and circuit-breakers.

Tomas (solutions): Proposed autoscale policy to include in SOW (plain language):
```
- committed_gpus: 12
- prewarm_count: 6
- burst_pool_max: 50 (consumes burst credits)
- autoscale_max: 120
- burst_credit_refill: 10 GPU-minutes/hour
- route_fallback: when queue latency > 180ms, route to quantized-chat model
- embedding_pool_sharing: embeddings may run on shared pool but flagged with lower priority
```
Note: burst_credit_refill controls long-run exposure. Adjust based on SLA economics.

Tom (sales): Customer asks: how do burst credits get billed if they regularly hit bursts? They want predictability.

Nina (acct-eng): Billing note to include: bursts beyond commit draw from prepaid burst credits (convertible to overage at lower of committed or on-demand price), and persistent overage (>30% of month) will trigger recommended commit increase and potential true-up. We'll add language: we monitor and notify.

Wei (eng-runtime): Security/tenancy note: Dedicated pools are tenant single-tenant; prewarm VMs/GPUs are still within tenant's pool so no cross-tenant cache exposure. For Private installs it's fully customer-managed. We can include audit logs and KMS integration in the SOW.

Tomas (solutions): SOW blurb draft for the customer: "We recommend an initial 12-GPU reserved commit, supplemented by a 6-instance prewarm pool and a burst-credit-enabled burst pool (up to 50 GPUs transient). Autoscaling will allow bursts to 120 GPUs with circuit-breakers that route high-latency requests to a quantized fallback model. We will monitor token distributions and recommend a monthly review to right-size the commit."

Tom (sales): Nice. Customer also wants an appendix showing cost delta between reserving 12 vs 24 GPUs. Can someone produce a quick cost model?

Nina (acct-eng): I'll prepare a simple table and include example monthly costs and Overage scenarios. Also include an explanation of prewarm pricing and burst-credit refill.

ops-bot: [note] ticket SF-4987 created for "enterprise commit cost modeling" assigned to Nina (acct-eng).

Tom (sales): Thanks team. I'll present this at tomorrow's call with their cloud procurement folks. If anything changes ping here."
